title: Assessing the impact of rehabilitation programs on aortic dissection patients and their quality of life
summary:
Aortic dissections, specifically Stanford type B, affect the descending aorta. They are a serious condition with a high variability in their progression, and pose a significant mortality risk. Despite early intervention, the condition can become chronic, meaning lifelong follow-up and management are required. 
Previous studies have shown impact on their everyday life, leading to a reduced quality of life compared to the general population. The reason for this is multifactorial, but patients being unsure into how to safely perform day to day activities plays a large part. 
The aim of this study is to better understand the rehabilitation process and the experiences of those who pass through the system and to compare this to the experiences of the clinical staff who run these programmes. To be able to achieve this the study is split into two parts. 
Firstly, patients with Type B aortic dissection will be interviewed following rehabilitation. This approach will provide detailed insights and help identify the everyday challenges that need to be addressed. Subsequently, questionnaires will be distributed to clinical staff in rehabilitation centers to collect additional quantitative data, enabling a comparison of their experiences with those of the patients

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patient Interviews: Adult, consent-capable patients who were hospitalized at the Heidelberg University Hospital between January 2014 and December 2024 for the treatment of Stanford Type B aortic dissection. 
Questionnaire Survey for staff at Rehabilitation Centers: Rehabilitation centers currently accredited for the treatment of Stanford Type B aortic dissections.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients under the age of 18, those who are unable to provide informed consent, and individuals with insufficient proficiency in the German language will be excluded from the interviews. The exclusion criterion for participation in the interviews is the absence of informed consent.
For the questionnaire-based survey in the second phase of the study, the only exclusion criterion is the lack of consent from the rehabilitation center.
